title: Geo contracting guidelines for sovereign customers
body:
Purpose:
This doc is an operational + contracting playbook for customers who require geographic guarantees ("region pinning") as part of a sovereign deployment. It sits between Legal, Sales, and Engineering: defines the clauses we are willing to accept, the technical acceptance criteria we must verify, and the operator-level runbook to validate evidence during onboarding and renewal.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: sales engineering, solutions engineering, legal, onboarding SREs, account managers.
- Scope: Hosted/Dedicated/Private with region-specific data anchoring requirements. Not intended for cross-border data residency legal analysis (Legal owns that), but provides contract language patterns and technical checks.

Summary (one-paragraph):
Customers frequently ask for contractual language that guarantees data will remain within a set of jurisdictions (e.g., EU-only, UK-only, AU-only). For Redwood offerings these guarantees are implemented via a combination of region pinning at request-routing level, dedicated capacity placement, and optional tenant-level escrow. This playbook lists our default negotiation positions, the minimum technical acceptance tests, evidence artifacts we provide, and escalation paths for exceptional requests.

Default negotiation positions (redlines Legal will accept unless flagged):
- Commitment: Redwood will route production inference requests and persistent customer assets (model checkpoints, embeddings storage, logs with PII) only to datacenters within the agreed territory. (We identify territory by cloud region codes and a canonical region list attached to SOW.)
- Exceptions: Transient caching (ephemeral KV caches <24h) may run outside territory for performance, but will never persist PII beyond territory boundaries.
- Subprocessors: Redwood will list cloud provider regions and any third-party vendors that may access telemetry; updates to that list will be provided 30 days prior to change.
- Audit rights: Customer may request on-prem or third-party audit evidence (SOC/ISO reports) and we will provide operator-run evidence packages (see "evidence bundle" below).
- Escrow & escrow triggers: For extremely sensitive customers we can offer regional escrow of deserialized data anchors — see Finance/Legal for pricing and escrow template.

Tech acceptance criteria (minimums we must verify before countersigning):
- Tenant pin configuration validated in staging and prod: requests tagged with tenant-region header must be honored 99.5% of the time across a 7-day synthetic traffic window. (Ticketed runbook: RES-412).
- Model artifacts and embeddings storage located in pinned region(s) (S3 buckets or object store region tags verified).
- Logs containing PII are routed to customer-specific secure bucket in territory or redacted at ingress.
- No egress to non-territory backups unless explicitly requested and documented.
- Cross-region failover behaviour documented: for customers that allow read-only failover, we will list which endpoints are used and timeouts after which failover triggers.

Operator verification checklist (onboarding):
1) Confirm canonical region list in SOW matches region tags used by infra (cloud console snapshot).
2) Deploy tenant to dedicated pool or apply strict routing policy for hosted tenants.
3) Run synthetic traffic across 72 hours with controlled locality variation to measure misroutes; capture anomalies.
4) Verify model storage: export object listing and assert region tag = agreed region. Attach export to evidence bundle.
5) Confirm log pipeline: ingestion points, processors, and storage destination for any PII-bearing logs.
6) Run telemetry sampling to ensure prefix/KV caches do not leak persisted payloads to other regions.
7) Provide final evidence bundle to customer (see below) and mark onboarding ticket as "residency-verified".

Evidence bundle contents (what we hand over):
- Cloud provider region snapshot (console export) and object-store listing (CSV).
- Routing policy config (policy file + applied cluster IDs).
- Synthetic test report (misroute %, timestamps, raw traces).
- Operator check signoffs (name, date, short notes).
- Redacted logs sample showing PII retention path (if requested).

SLA & fallback semantics to include in SOW:
- Residency SLA: Redwood guarantees that >= 99.5% of requests remain within agreed territory over rolling 30-day window; SLA credits tied to verified misroute events.
- Failover model: by default Redwood will not perform cross-territory failover for pinned customers unless a separate cross-region disaster recovery appendix is signed.
- Partial service windows: in the event of regional outage Redwood may route read-only operations to adjacent regions only after customer approval or per emergency clause (we maintain an emergency phone/email triage list).

Sample contract clause language (starter text for Legal):
"Redwood will, subject to the terms of this Agreement, ensure that Customer Data and Customer Models are stored and processed within the geographic territory set forth in Schedule A (the \"Territory\"). Redwood will not intentionally transfer Customer Data outside the Territory except as expressly permitted in this Agreement or requested by Customer in writing. Redwood will maintain technical controls and operational processes to evidence compliance and will provide the evidence bundle described in Appendix B upon reasonable request."

Edge cases and escalation patterns (when Sales/Legal should loop Eng):
- Customer requires explicit prohibition on caching outside territory for any request: engineering must review feasibility (may require dedicated pools or code changes).
- Customer asks for guaranteed single-region routing even during zone maintenance: escalate to infra + capacity planning for dedicated pool sizing and maintenance blackout windows.
- Requests for per-request cryptographic attestation of region locality: route to Research/Applied-ML for feasibility and Legal for contract language.

Customer communication templates (sales + AM talking points):
- Quick email snippet: "We can guarantee that your inference requests and persisted artifacts are anchored within the [Territory]. We'll provide a technical evidence bundle and perform a 72-hour validation run during onboarding. For emergency DR we will only fail over across borders with written approval. See attached appendix for details."
- Executive summary: 1 page evidence + checklist delivered post-onboarding, follow-up cadence (30/90/365 days).

Operational costs and pricing hints (for Sales/Finance):
- Dedicated pools typically add 15–40% markup depending on capacity reservation length and region (APAC premiums higher).
- Escrow/attestation services and additional audit packaging are billable add-ons.
- For small customers, a standardized "territory package" (single-region S3 + routing policy + 72-hour test) is the lowest friction offering.

Open questions / things to decide (work items):
- Do we want a standard "Territory Definition" table for each major market (EU, UK, AU, CA) that Legal can reference? (owner: Nora, due: 2025-03-01)
- Standardized evidence retention windows: how long do we keep the evidence bundle on our side? (ops suggestion: 2 years)
- Billing taxonomy: should we create a distinct SKU for "region-pinned tenancy" to automate quoting? (Finance + Product)
- Mechanism for automated misroute alerts to customers and internal SRE team (ticket: RES-412)

Next steps / immediate todos:
- Legal to produce template Appendix B (evidence bundle language) and share v1 for review (Nora).
- SE to run one regression against the EU anchor pilot tenant this week and attach results to RES-412. (Ethan/Jill).
- Product to propose SKU and list pricing bands for dedicated region runs by 2025-02-28.

Notes to self / brainstorm fragments (working):
- Could we offer "logical residency" where we encrypt payloads with customer-owned keys before leaving region — mitigates some audit concerns but still counts as transfer; may be acceptable to some customers.
- Consider per-tenant telemetry tax (small recurring fee) to cover extended retention of audit artifacts.
- For very large enterprise deals, propose an on-prem private control plane with a small Redwood-managed agent in-customer-datacenter for verification hooks.

Links I used while drafting:
- RES-412 (region pinning testbed): https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RES-412
- Onboarding checklist template (internal): s3://redwood-templates/onboarding/residency-checklist-v2.csv

If you're reviewing: please annotate open questions inline and tag the appropriate owner. This is intentionally pragmatic (not legalese) — Legal will convert to contract-ready language but needs the tech acceptance criteria to bind the commitments.

-- Ethan
